items.fact: Card 060's preparation, on mock only, through operator.run(backend='mock', root=<scratch root>). Three scratch roots under D:/sma-scratch/060/roots: A_today (a byte copy of today's envelope/safety.json and snapshot.json, which hold no focus limit and no pfs_not_engaged), B_limits (A plus TEST focus_z_10x and focus_z_20x limits, 0 to 9000 um) and C_limits_pfs (B plus a TEST pfs_not_engaged, PFS.State in [TEST_off]). Every envelope limit, focus-hold reading, approval and camera ceiling in these runs that is not the person's is a TEST value under D:/sma-scratch/060 and says so in its own note. None is a fact about the instrument, and none left scratch.

items.how: All five focus plans pass every check but 88 against this repository (validate.py given their scratch paths), and 88 fails each for the missing focus_z limit, correctly. Against the TEST envelope B, check 88 passes 001-004 and fails 005 by design. 001 (no limit) and 005 (above the max) can never pass check 88, so they are run from scratch, cited here by sha256, and never committed. 002-004 are copied into questions/ on the day, after the person writes the limits, as revision 2 with range_um set inside them. 006 is a dry-run candidate, not a bench plan.

items.fact: With the plans as they would go to the bench, the camera ceiling a gap because the store has no full-scale count, 001, 002, 003 and 005 all refused 'focus search not started: camera_ceiling is the gap', and NONE showed the refusal it exists to show. 004 refused as not approved. No Z command went out in any, and Z read 2050 um before and after each.
items.how: operator.py:1315-1321 builds the decider, which refuses on a gap ceiling, BEFORE orchestrator.py:1468-1506 checks the hand-over lens, the limits, the range, the read-back criterion and focus hold. So on Thursday, unless the camera count is entered in the store and the plans revised to cite it before steps 1-2, every focus refusal the person watches is the ceiling's. Either the bench order changes (step 5 first, then a librarian entry, then revised plans) or the decider is built after the gate's pre-move checks; the second is a code change in Microscope 1's files.

No plan path turns the transmitted lamp and the Aura on today, so the abort-run plan was not committed. Candidate A, naming the registry's dia_lamp and widefield_source_a, was refused whole by the software-motion check (orchestrator.py:1021-1032). Candidate B, naming the Micro-Manager labels DiaLamp and Aura, passed that check and was refused at preflight: 'Aura' is neither a channel nor an element. Past both, nothing would be written: derive_commands (operator.py:999-1023) builds an action's params from numbers[] only, never `settings`, and apply() writes only `settings` (devices/micromanager.py:428-438, devices/mock.py:58). Live view sets DiaLamp and refuses the Aura (operator.py:1433-1434). A plan also has no step that keeps a run open for the outside stop.
